latin.641: §. IV. Reformati Tertiam noviterque excogitatam Manducationem Corporis CHRISTI, Corporalem scilicet Oralemque, quæ tamen merè Supernaturalis, nec ullo modo Naturalis aut Physica sit, triplici argumentorum genere impugnant, quorum primum à Natura Corporis Christi manducandi; Alterum à Natura de jure Manducantium; Tertium denique à Manducationis ipsius Oralis natura. Cuncta ex ipsâ S. Scripturâ petita sunt & hujus testimoniis innituntur.
latin.642: Ad PRIMUM Argumentorum GENUS pertinet. (1) Corpus Christi in Cœna S. manducandum, esse Cibum merè Spiritualem, non Corporalem, solius Animæ, non Corporis, in animæ tantùm, non Corporis etiam alimoniam cessurum, etiamsi per alimoniam hanc animæ, in Corpus quoque, ob arctissimam cum anima Unionem, eóque in totum hominem, utilitas eximia, per & post resurrectionem à mortuis se exsertura, redundet; At Cibus merè spiritualis, Corporaliter, etiam quà Os tantùm, manducari, i. e. Ori imponi, nequit, quin hôc ipsô, si Cibus sit, evadat Cibus Corporalis, Cibus verò Corporalis Ore receptus, nec eôdem emissus, denique abit in ventrem, cibus sic ex toto Corporalis evasurus; Quicquid intrat in os, abit in Ventrem, Matth. 15, 17. Esca Ventri & Venter escis, 1. Cor. 6, 13. Consentiunt hactenus Pontificii, Corpus Christi, ex pane transmutatum, eô ipsô quòd manducatur, non in os tantùm, sed & in ventrem seu stomachum recipi. Porrò ventre receptus cibus, in secessum ex parte emittitur, juxta aliud, quod Matth. 15, 17. additur à Christo: Nondum intelligitis, quicquid intruditur in Os, in Ventrem ingredi & in latrinam ejici. Consequentiam abnuentibus quidem Pontificiis postremam, & Stercoranistis hæreticis imputantibus, sed frustrà, utpote ab ipso Christo nexam.
latin.643: (2) Corpus Christi in Cœna manducandum, sub certo ac definito schemate suo, i. e. sub schemate Passionis & Mortis manducandum esse: Sic enim Christus: Hoc est Corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur & in mortem datur, Luc. 22, 19. Non quod pro vobis natum aut enutritum est, licèt non minùs pro nobis natum ac enutritum, quàm crucifixum & in mortem traditum intelligatur. Ut ridiculè irrideant adversarii argumentum, To quod, in quatenus convertens, nisi ipsum Christum ridiculè locutum, i. e. crucifixi Corporis sui mentionem, citra peculiarem in hoc ipsum respectum, blasphement fecisse. At sub crucifixionis mortisque schemate, Corpus Christi Corporaliter Oraliterque manducari non potest, utpote (sub hoc schemate nullibi ampliùs corporaliter præsens Rom. 6, 9.); Bene autem Spiritualiter: ut proinde jubeamur disertè, quotiescunque de pane, qui sacramentaliter Corpus Christi est, manducamus, mortem Domini memoriâ recolere, i. e. animâ volvere & aliis notam facere. (3) Corpus Christi in Cœna manducandum, Sacramenti Cœnæ, ex duabus partibus, per naturam Sacramenti, Signô scil. & Signato constantis, eam partem absolvere, quam Signatum vocant, per panem ceu Signum significatum; At Significati ea natura est, juxta Augustinum, ut per signum sensui obvium, soli intellectui innotescat: Quod verò soli intellectui manifestum sit, id oraliter accipi ac manducari non potest, utpote hôc ipsô sensui exponendum, atque eatenus signati naturâ exuendum.
latin.644: SECUNDUM Argumentorum GENUS, duplices manducantes sistit, Orali Manducationi Corporis Christi in Cœna, infensos infestósque: Ex unâ parte Christum Dominum jubentem manducare, qui & ipse manducasse, pronâ satis consequentiâ ex Matth. 26, 29. Marc. 14, 24. 25. & Luc. 22, 15. 16. colligitur, adstipulantibus Patribus, Hieronymo in Epist. ad Hedibiam Quæst. 2. August. lib. 2. de Doctrina Christiana cap. 3. Chrysostomo Hom. 83. in Matth. At Christum Corpus suum proprium, Oraliter manducasse, multis nominibus absurdum est, Vid. Burmann. Disput. XVII. de Cœna, num. 104. Dixeris: non minùs absurdum, Christum spiritualiter Corpus suum manducasse. Resp. Spiritualis manducandi Corpus Christi modus, expressè in Scriptura traditus Joh. 6. non item Oralis, de quâ altum in Scriptura silentium, manducatio licèt ipsa quà rem & absolutè, expressis verbis, in ipsâ S. Cœnæ institutione, injuncta legatur. (2) Spiritualis Corporis Christi manducandi modus, varius esse potest, alius in Christum, alius in nos competens; Non item Oralis, ubique quà rem, unus idemque, à quocunque peragatur. Christus crucifixum Corpus suum, seu crucifigendum, quatenus crucifigendum, spiritualiter manducavit, Se, passionem mortemque suam nobis communicando harumque fructum & efficaciam addicendo imputandóque; Nos Christi Corpus spiritualiter manducamus, vera vivaque fide ipsum totum cum meritis suis omnibus amplectendo, i. e. eorum participes fiendo. Ex alterâ parte, jussos manducare, h. e. ad Christianam fidem conversos, ut hinc hodieque Infideles omnes à Cœnæ S. participatione arceantur; & quidem tales Conversos ad Christianam fidem, qui seipsos probant, i. e. qui in Statu pœnitentiæ & habitu fidei vivæ consistunt, exclusis impœnitentibus & impiis. 1. Cor. 11, 28. At nulla ratio alia prostat, ob quam impœnitentes à Cœna S. abstinere debeant, quam quòd spiritualiter Corpus Christi manducare non possunt, fide salvificâ destituti, Oralis interim Manducationis cum fidelibus Christi discipulis juxta capaces.
latin.645: TERTIUM Argumentorum GENUS ex ipsius Manducationis, in S. Cœna instituendæ, Natura fluit, quæ si Corporalis Oralisque corporis Christi statuatur, (1) deprehenditur hujusmodi, ut à Christo institui haud potuerit, partim quòd anthropophagían inducit & haimatoposían, Deo Hominique abominabilem, Levit. 7, 26. & cap. 17, 14. partim quòd Diaspasin inter Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, cui obnoxia ampliùs esse nequeunt, incautè admittit, cum pane corpus Christi absque sanguine, cum vino verò sanguinem absque corpore, oraliter accipi subinnuens; partim denique, quòd Christi tàm Corpori, quam sanguini, quin ipsi toti, contumeliosè accidit: Enimverò contumeliosum, (a) Christum gloriosum redigere in & sub elementa panis & Vini, ceu sub claustrum. (b) Christum semel crucifixum, passum & mortuum, in novam aliquam passionis scenam reducere, Corpusque ejus & sanguinem ori humano intrudere manducanda Oraliter bibendáque. (c) Dicere Carnem Christi sacrosanctam sanguinemque ejus, non solùm fidelium piorumque, sed & impiorum ac infidelium impura ora subintrare, adeóque profanum quemque Nebulonem, qui Diabolum quotidie in corde & ore gerit, verè tamen Christi quoque Corpus & sanguinem usurpare. Vide Zwingerum, Declarat. sent. Orthod. de Cœna Thesi 25.
latin.646: (2) Sensualis foret, seu gustui exposita, quia omnis cibus, oraliter manducatus, sentitur manducari; sed Corpus Christi nemo hactenus sensit à se manducari, ne fidelis quidem Christóque mysticè unitus, quotiescunque etiam, quantâque fide & persuasione, arctiorem cum Christo Communionem consequendi, Cœnam S. accessit. Quin Capernaitica foret, eô ipsô, quia Oralis, quandoquidem sic Corporalis & Carnalis eóque Capernaitica, sive immediatè, sive mediante pane, fiat; sive physicô, sive hyperphysicô modô perficiatur; sive momentanea sit inque ore desinat, sive cum mora temporis ad guttur tandemque ad stomachum, manducatum deferatur. (3) Sola & per se considerata (a) non valet quicquam, Johan. 6, 63. he de sarx ouk ophelei ouden dicit Christus; Vult verò, non carnem suam per se spectatam, nihil quicquam valere, sed, vel carnem in oppositione Spiritûs, vel, si caro Christi respicitur, intelligitur caro Christi tam Capernaiticè & Oraliter, quàm tantùm Sacramentaliter comesta: sic enim Theophylactus in hunc locum: he de sarx tout’ esti to sarkikôs auta endechesthai, ouden ophelei, Et Zwinglius noster in eundem: Caro CHRISTI plurimùm omnino, imò immensum prodest, sed casa, non carnaliter ambesa. Casa nos servat à cæde, non, carnaliter manducata. (b) Non vivificat, sive sit panis, sive carnis Christi, cum, vel sine pane: Oralis Manducatio panis, non potest vivificare: hoc enim est opus solius Dei; Nec carnis Christi Manducatio propria vivificat; hanc enim cùm Capernaitæ intelligerent, respondet Christus. Spiritus est qui vivificat, Caro non prodest quicquam.

pass_a.641: §. IV. The Reformed impugn by a triple kind of arguments the Third and newly devised Eating of CHRIST’s Body — namely the Corporal and Oral, which yet is merely Supernatural and in no way Natural or Physical — of which the first is from the Nature of Christ’s Body to be eaten; the Second from the Nature of those who by right are Eaters; and finally the Third from the nature of the Oral Eating itself. All are sought from Sacred Scripture itself and rest on its testimonies.
pass_a.642: To the FIRST GENUS of Arguments belongs: (1) That Christ’s Body to be eaten in the Sacred Supper is a merely Spiritual Food, not Corporal — of the Soul alone, not of the Body — destined to be nourishment of the soul only, not also of the Body, even if through this soul-nourishment an exceeding utility also overflows into the Body and so into the whole man, by reason of the closest Union with the soul, to show itself through and after the resurrection from the dead; But a merely spiritual Food cannot be eaten Corporaliter, even as to the Mouth alone — i.e. placed in the Mouth — without by that very act, if it is Food, becoming Corporal Food; and Corporal Food received by the Mouth and not emitted by the same finally goes into the belly, food thus about to become Corporal altogether; Whatever enters into the mouth goes away into the Belly, Matt. 15:17. Food for the Belly and the Belly for foods, 1 Cor. 6:13. The Pontiffs thus far agree that Christ’s Body, transmuted from bread, by the very fact that it is eaten is received not into the mouth alone but also into the belly or stomach. Further, food received in the belly is in part emitted into the privy, according to what else Christ adds in Matt. 15:17: Do you not yet understand that whatever is thrust into the Mouth enters the Belly and is cast out into the latrine. The Pontiffs indeed deny the last consequence and impute it to the Stercoranist heretics — but in vain, seeing it is tied by Christ Himself.
pass_a.643: (2) That Christ’s Body to be eaten in the Supper is to be eaten under its certain and definite schema — i.e. under the schema of the Passion and Death: For so Christ: This is my Body, which is broken for you and given unto death, Luke 22:19. Not which was born or nourished for you — although it is understood no less born and nourished for us than crucified and delivered unto death. So that the adversaries ridiculously mock the argument converting ‘which’ into ‘inasmuch as,’ unless they blaspheme that Christ Himself spoke ridiculously — i.e. made mention of His crucified Body without peculiar respect to this very thing. But under the schema of crucifixion and death Christ’s Body cannot be eaten Corporaliter and Oraliter, seeing that under this schema it is nowhere any longer corporally present (Rom. 6:9); But well Spiritualiter: so that we are therefore expressly commanded, as often as we eat of the bread which is sacramentally Christ’s Body, to recall the Lord’s death by memory — i.e. to turn it in the soul and make it known to others. (3) That Christ’s Body to be eaten in the Supper completes that part of the Supper’s Sacrament — consisting by the Sacrament’s nature of two parts, Sign and Signified — which they call the Signified, signified through the bread as Sign; But the nature of the Signified, according to Augustine, is that through a sign obvious to sense it becomes known to the intellect alone: But what is manifest to the intellect alone cannot be orally received and eaten, seeing that by that very act it would have to be exposed to sense and so far stripped of the signified’s nature.
pass_a.644: The SECOND GENUS of Arguments sets forth double eaters hostile and adverse to the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body in the Supper: On one side the Lord Christ commanding to eat, who also Himself ate — gathered by ready enough consequence from Matt. 26:29, Mark 14:24–25, and Luke 22:15–16, the Fathers agreeing (Jerome to Hedibia Q. 2; Augustine On Christian Doctrine 2.3; Chrysostom Hom. 83 on Matt.). But that Christ ate His own Body Oraliter is absurd under many names — see Burmann Disput. XVII on the Supper n. 104. You will say: no less absurd that Christ ate His Body spiritually. Resp. The spiritual mode of eating Christ’s Body is expressly handed down in Scripture, John 6 — not likewise the Oral, about which there is deep silence in Scripture, although eating itself as to the thing and absolutely is read enjoined in express words in the Sacred Supper’s Institution. (2) The spiritual mode of eating Christ’s Body can be various — one fitting Christ, another us; Not likewise the Oral, everywhere as to the thing one and the same by whoever it is performed. Christ spiritually ate His crucified Body, or to-be-crucified inasmuch as to be crucified, by communicating Himself, His passion and death to us and assigning and imputing their fruit and efficacy; We spiritually eat Christ’s Body by embracing Him whole with all His merits by true living faith — i.e. becoming partakers of them. On the other side, those commanded to eat — i.e. converts to the Christian faith, that hence even today all Unbelievers are kept from participation of the Sacred Supper; and indeed such Converts who prove themselves, i.e. who stand in the State of penitence and habit of living faith, the impenitent and impious excluded (1 Cor. 11:28). But no other reason stands why the impenitent ought to abstain from the Sacred Supper than that they cannot spiritually eat Christ’s Body, destitute of saving faith — while meantime equally capable of Oral Eating with Christ’s faithful disciples.
pass_a.645: The THIRD GENUS of Arguments flows from the Nature of the Eating itself to be instituted in the Sacred Supper, which if it be stated Corporal and Oral of Christ’s body, (1) is found of such a kind that it could hardly have been instituted by Christ — partly because it introduces anthropophagy and blood-drinking, abominable to God and Man (Lev. 7:26 and ch. 17:14); partly because it incautiously admits a Diaspasis between Christ’s Body and Blood, to which they can no longer be liable, hinting that with the bread Christ’s body without blood, and with the wine blood without body, are orally received; and finally partly because it happens contumeliously to Christ’s Body and blood, nay to Himself whole: For truly it is contumelious (a) to reduce the glorious Christ into and under the elements of bread and Wine as under a lock; (b) to bring Christ once crucified, having suffered and died, back into some new scene of passion, and to thrust His Body and blood into the human mouth to be eaten Oraliter and drunk; (c) to say that Christ’s most holy Flesh and blood enter not only the mouths of the faithful and pious but also the impure mouths of the impious and unbelievers — and so that every profane Scoundrel who daily bears the Devil in heart and mouth truly yet also usurps Christ’s Body and blood. See Zwinger, Declarat. sent. Orthod. de Cœna Thesis 25.
pass_a.646: (2) It would be Sensual, or exposed to taste, because every food orally eaten is felt to be eaten; but no one has thus far felt Christ’s Body eaten by himself — not even the believer mystically united to Christ, however often and with how great faith and persuasion of obtaining closer Communion with Christ he has approached the Sacred Supper. Nay it would be Capernaite by the very fact that it is Oral, seeing that thus it is Corporal and Carnal and so Capernaite — whether immediately or by means of bread; whether finished in a physical or hyperphysical mode; whether momentary and ending in the mouth, or with delay of time the eaten is carried to the throat and at last to the stomach. (3) Considered alone and by itself (a) it avails nothing, John 6:63 — ‘but the flesh profits nothing,’ says Christ; Yet He wills not that His flesh viewed by itself avails nothing, but either flesh in opposition to the Spirit, or, if Christ’s flesh is regarded, Christ’s flesh eaten as Capernaitically and Oraliter as only Sacramentally is understood: for so Theophylact on this place: ‘but the flesh — that is, to receive them fleshly — profits nothing,’ And our Zwingli on the same: CHRIST’s Flesh profits very much indeed, nay immensely — but slain, not carnally chewed. Slain it saves us from slaughter, not carnally eaten. (b) It does not vivify, whether it be of bread or of Christ’s flesh, with or without bread: Oral Eating of bread cannot vivify — for this is the work of God alone; Nor does the proper Eating of Christ’s flesh vivify; for when the Capernaites understood this, Christ answers: It is the Spirit that vivifies; the Flesh profits nothing.

641: §.IV: the Reformed attack the third newly invented Eating of Christ’s Body — corporal and oral, yet claimed merely supernatural, not natural/physical.
Three argument genera from Scripture: (1) nature of the Body to be eaten; (2) nature of those who by right eat; (3) nature of Oral eating itself.
642: FIRST genus (1): the Body in the Supper is merely spiritual food for the soul — not corporal food for the body (though soul-nourishment overflows to the whole man after resurrection).

A merely spiritual food cannot be mouthed corporally without becoming corporal food that goes to the belly (Matt. 15:17; 1 Cor. 6:13). Pontiffs agree it reaches the stomach; Christ’s own latrine-clause they vainly shove onto Stercoranists.
643: FIRST (2): it is to be eaten under the Passion/Death schema (‘broken for you / given unto death’) — not as merely born/nourished. Under crucifixion’s schema the Body is nowhere still corporally present (Rom. 6:9); it is well eaten spiritually, and we are told to remember the Lord’s death.
FIRST (3): as Signatum of the sacrament it is known to the intellect alone through the sense-sign (Augustine) — so it cannot be orally received without ceasing to be signified.
644: SECOND genus: two hostile ‘eaters.’ Christ commanded eating and Himself ate (Matt./Mark/Luke; Fathers) — yet that He ate His own Body orally is absurd (Burmann). Spiritual eating is in John 6; Oral is deep Scripture-silence.

Spiritual mode can differ for Christ (communicating passion’s fruit) and for us (living faith). Converts in penitence are bidden; the impenitent are barred only because they cannot eat spiritually — while still as able as the faithful for Oral, if Oral were the issue (1 Cor. 11:28).
645: THIRD genus (1): if Supper-eating is corporal-oral of Christ’s body, Christ could hardly have instituted it — it imports anthropophagy and blood-drinking (Lev. 7; 17), and a careless split of Body from Blood with bread/wine.

It also contumeliously locks the glorious Christ under bread and wine, reopens a passion-scene by thrusting Body and blood into human mouths, and has the holy Flesh enter even the impure mouths of the impious (Zwinger, Thesis 25).
646: THIRD (2)–(3): Oral would be sensual (felt by taste) — yet no one, not even the mystic believer, has ever felt Christ’s Body eaten. By being Oral it is Capernaite — whether immediate or through bread, physical or hyperphysical, mouth-only or down to the stomach.

Alone it avails nothing (Jn 6:63): Theophylact and Zwingli read ‘flesh profits nothing’ of Capernaite/oral (or merely sacramental) chewing — slain flesh saves; carnal chewing does not vivify. Stop mid-§.IV (exception / further genera remain).
